full_judgment:
7. It is contended by Dr. Kamal Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, that having regard to provisions of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in particular Articles 7, 19, 21, 27, 31,144 and 145 has respondent No. 1 lawful authority to allot, lease land owned by the Government to a party in an arbitrary manner without following any procedure such as public notice or public tender or public auction which would give all citizens equal opportunity? The learned Advocate further submitted that where the land in question was shown in the Master Plan as reserved for car park can the Government functionaries without following the statutory requirement for alteration of the Master Plan, allot the said land for a different purpose disregarding the prevailing market rate? According to the learned Advocate, this being a question of general public importance should be decided by this Court. 

 8. Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 7, on the other hand, has contended that there was no necessity for interpretation of Article 144 of the Constitution inasmuch as the said Article is merely an enabling power of the Government like a private owner to deal with Government properties. According to the learned Advocate there, is no question of public importance involved in the decision of the suit and even if such question is raised the Court of Assistant Judge can decide the question which may ultimately be raised before this Court in revisional jurisdiction. 

 11. Dr. Kamal Hossain submitted that the executive authority of the Republic has been enjoined with the power of acquisition and disposal of Government land by Article 144 of the Constitution. According to the learned Advocate, the executive authority cannot deal with Government properties like a private individual and the question would naturally arise in the suit whether the executive authority acted within its bounds as prescribed by the constitution, the law, the rule and procedure, if any, and to find out the authority of the respondent Nos. 1 to 6 in dealing with the suit land and, as such, it involves the question of the interpretation of Article 144 of the Constitution.
